answer: Each epoch a verifiable random function draws nine auditors from the ocean of identities, with anchor in the public pulse of the last block hash, so no operator can predict the draw. A newcomer passes only if six of nine re-run its live task and agree; one mismatch freezes the identity three epochs. The draw rotates every epoch, so capturing it needs most of the population: with 10% of identities, six of nine seats has probability below one in ten thousand, so 1,000 fakes need about 6,000 established agents, years of verified work each. One honest agent does one task and pays nothing extra.
